newsitem.title: USA: SEC may ease mutual fund disclosure rules - NYT.
newsitem.headline: SEC may ease mutual fund disclosure rules - NYT.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission might loosen a rule requiring mutual funds to disclose all the securities held in a portfolio to shareholders, the New York Times said on Tuesday.
The SEC was considering whether to permit mutual funds to list their top 25 to 50 holdings instead, the newspaper said.

Barry Barbash, director of the SEC's division of investment management, which regulates mutual funds, told a conference in California that the proposed changes were part of a plan to revamp mutual fund shareholder reports, the daily said.
The list of top holdings would be accompanied by a graphic illustration of the fund's involvement in various industries or geographic regions, the Times said.
